failure.reason: EOFError: Compressed file ended before the end-of-stream marker was reached

gzip.strict_reader_error: EOFError: Compressed file ended before the end-of-stream marker was reached
gzip.footer_note: No valid gzip EOF/footer was reached. The CRC shown is only the computed available-prefix CRC and is not a successful member integrity check.

flow: open_path_trace opens gzip directly on the final workspace path in exclusive text mode
complete_perp.ResearchExchange._record updates in-memory count/rolling and writes each corresponding 10-field line to the retained text stream
driver sets PATH_TRACE=None, calls trace.close(), then calls path_trace_receipt on the pathname
The failed receipt contains the complete path_trace_receipt structure and readback EOFError; this control flow shows trace.close returned normally
readback hashes/stat-checks the pathname and parses gzip rows, but the old writer does not retain/publish an immutable spool or compare open-FD versus pathname device/inode

established_findings: The actual pathname is a stable truncated gzip member matching the failed receipt bytes and SHA.
The file contains 644756 intact consecutive lines but ends in a partial next line before the expected checkpoint count.
147543 measurement points are missing relative to the checkpoint, so supplying a gzip footer cannot restore evidence.
The producer correctly marked the segment failed and non-resumable. These flags and original files must remain unchanged.

root_cause_boundary.confirmed: Evidence stream publication/readback failed to preserve the complete expected path up to the checkpoint. The surviving pathname stops before the producer checkpoint.
not_proven: Which process or filesystem mechanism caused the truncation
Whether the original open file descriptor referred to a replaced/unlinked inode, because the failed producer recorded no open-FD identity
Whether a workspace synchronization/copy operation caused the surviving earlier prefix
root_cause_boundary.fsync_limit: Lack of fsync alone normally concerns crash durability and does not explain a successful close followed by immediate pathname readback of a much earlier prefix without a crash. An FD/path replacement or publication-visibility race is compatible with the evidence, but attribution is not established.

minimal_fix.scope: Change evidence I/O only; preserve economic decisions, events, schedule and all count/rolling checks.
steps: Write each segment gzip to SpooledTemporaryFile(max_size=64MiB), with an anonymous temporary file on spill, rather than a long-lived workspace pathname.
Pass the spool explicitly as GzipFile(fileobj=...). Close TextIO/gzip to finalize compressed data while retaining the spool for rewind/read; avoid calling spool.fileno() before spill is desired.

After finalization, exclusively publish the complete compressed bytes into the new run directory, flush/fsync, verify the publishing FD and pathname identify the same file, then run the unchanged full gzip/count/rolling readback.
Fail closed on any replacement, truncation, CRC, row/count or rolling mismatch. Do not repair or flip flags on the failed original segment.
Register the changed producer under a new spec/run directory and start both arms anew; preserve this failed run as evidence.
directed_validation: Old and new writer receive identical deterministic lines; their fully decoded bytes must match exactly. gzip headers and compressed SHA need not match.
Replace/truncate the workspace publication path during the targeted test; publication must reject it or the private spool must remain unaffected, with no false passed receipt.
Use a deliberately small threshold to exercise anonymous-file spill and verify identical decoded bytes and count/rolling validation.
